pr_title: Bluetooth: ISO: Add TS flag to ISO recv
pr_body:
Add a flag to tell the application that the timestamp value is valid. 

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/44283

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: ISO: Add TS flag for ISO receive
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently we use `0` to indicate that no timestamp was set by the controller. However `0` is a valid timestamp, so this is a poor choice.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We already have a `flags` field that we can extend to add a `ts_valid` flag. It needs to be converted into a bitfield for this to work. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We can alternatively add a separate `ts_valid` flag to avoid changing existing code. 

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments:
These three are mutual exclusive - hence not sure it should be 3 individual bits, but rather a 2-bit value in a bitfield and a separate enum - like before.
For example:
```
...
uint8_t flags_status : 2
uint8_t flags_time_stamp : 1
...
```
Maybe you can even use the enum as the type - very old C-standards did not allow this, but I think more resent will - I believe it will generate an error if it does not.

@Casper-Bonde-Bose I don't think mutually exclusive bits in a bitfield is a problem, but perhaps it should be documented? 

I did consider changing this to an enum as well. 

Regarding changing the field in the struct to 2 bitfield values, I think that is something we've generally avoided in the host, and have earlier been told not to do that, and to use macros instead. @jhedberg @Vudentz Any of you can chime in here why we avoid e.g. `uint8_t flags : 2;`? 

One alternative to this change is to leave the current flags as is, and add a `bool valid_ts` instead.

I would prefer either bit-filed in the structure or separate members. Maybe the latter would be the "simple" solution that allows use of enum type for the status - without the need to look into if all compilers support this? 
Status flag should not be of type `uint_8` but the enum in both cases.

Changing the type of the packet status can be done, but I'd rather do that in a separate PR if we decide to simply add a new field for the TS validity. 

I'd like to get feedback from one other person regarding this (@jhedberg @asbjornsabo ?), as this approach is not any different than e.g. the `struct k_work.flags` 

Basically the three options are

1) What this PR proposes:
```c
uint8_t flags; /* both status flags and a TS valid flag */
```

2) 
New bool/flag for TS valid
```c
uint8_t flags; /* unchanged */
bool ts_valid;
```

3)
Using the C-style bitfields 
```c
uint8_t flags_status : 2;
uint8_t flags_ts_valid : 1;
```
I don't mind it being a single flags field, since it keeps the struct simpler, but I'll leave this up to you.
IMHO for consistency in host APIs, single flags field as already in this PR is good for me.

(I Approved before reading this discussion.)
I see Casper's point, and consider it as valid.  Having a bitfield often implies that one can set any combination of bits.
Alternative 2. is in that sense the cleanest.  But it does also seem a bit clunky, as one gets two variables for communicating the status.
Alternative 1 should be OK, if well documented.
(I do not see a need for 3.)
